newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZCC says Radio Network NZ can't buy Fifeshire FM.
newsitem.headline: NZCC says Radio Network NZ can't buy Fifeshire FM.

text.p: New Zealand's anti-monopolies Commerce Commission on Friday said it had declined to clear Radio Network of New Zealand Ltd to buy Fifeshire FM Broadcasters Ltd.

Chairman Alan Bollard said in a statement the commission was not satisfied that the proposal would not result in the acquisition of a dominant position in the market for radio advertising services in Nelson.
Bollard said the proposal involved The Radio Network acquiring all of the radio stations and frequencies owned by Fifeshire in Nelson, Westport and Picton.
"The Radio Network already operates in these markets. If the acquisition had proceeded, Radio Network would control 99 percent of the Nelson radio advertising market," Bollard said.
The commission concluded that existing customers and remaining competitors would not constrain the merged company.
"The commission considers that while new entry into the Nelson radio advertising market is technically possible, it is not commercially viable or likely," Bollard said.
